before: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency is described as the most common enzyme deficiency worldwide and is an X-linked inherited disorder that most commonly affects persons of African, Asian, Mediterranean, or Middle-Eastern descent [1].

Familial Mediterranean fever is a monogenic autoinflammatory disorder caused by mutations in the MEFV gene that mainly affects people of Mediterranean descent, with higher incidence in Turkish, Jewish, Arabic, and Armenian populations [2].

A separate consortium analysis combined MEFV gene results and clinical findings from 27,504 patients across 35 institutions in Turkey and Northern Cyprus to examine genotype-phenotype correlation [2].
The study identified 51 families with multilocus pathogenic variation, mostly driven by runs of homozygosity reflecting genomic segments identical-by-descent [3].

MEFV variants and familial Mediterranean fever

Familial Mediterranean fever is a monogenic autoinflammatory disorder caused by mutations in the MEFV gene that mainly affects people of Mediterranean descent, with higher incidence in Turkish, Jewish, Arabic, and Armenian populations [7].

A separate consortium analysis combined MEFV gene results and clinical findings from 27,504 patients across 35 institutions in Turkey and Northern Cyprus to examine genotype-phenotype correlation [7].
The study identified 51 families with multilocus pathogenic variation, mostly driven by runs of homozygosity reflecting genomic segments identical-by-descent [8].
